(The deposition commenced: 12:22 p.m.) 
GLORIA JEAN BROWN, Deponent, of 
180 Dogwood Drive, Bridgeport, Connecticut 
06606, being first duly sworn by Bethany A.

testified on her oath as follows:

entries.speaker: THE COURT REPORTER
entries.text:
Usual 
stipulations?

entries.speaker: HEADING
entries.text:
DIRECT EXAMINATION
BY MR. KUMAR:

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Good afternoon, Ms. Brown.

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Good afternoon.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
My name is Dimple Kumar. I'm going to be asking 
you a series of questions today. But before I ask you 
questions, there's just a few instructions, I'm sure your 
attorney has gone over them with you, but just as a 
reminder we do this with everyone. So please one 
important instruction is please let me completely finish 
my question before you respond. That way we're not 
speaking over each other. Okay?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Okay. Yes.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Head nods, head gestures in normal conversation 
are okay. But just for today's purposes, please follow up 
that with some verbal response to my question. Okay?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Okay.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
If you don't understand a question -- I'm not 
trying to trick you in any way -- just let me know you 
don't understand it and I'll be happy to rephrase it in a 
way that you can understand it. Okay?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yes.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Okay. And any time you want to take a break, 
just let me know. I ask that you answer the last question 
I ask before you take a break.

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yes. I understand.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
In preparation of this deposition today, did you 
review any paper documents?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: No.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Okay. Are you presently on any medications?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: What? What medications are those?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: I take -- is it -- I think it's pregabalin.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Anything else?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Like a 5 milligram for high blood pressure.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: What's the pregabalin for?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Nerves.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: And when were you first prescribed that?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
It was after the accident when I started seeing 
Dr. Saba. I started having pain in my back and going into 
my legs.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
We're going to get to the accident, of course. 
So I just have a few background questions before we get to 
the accident.
How old are you today, ma'am?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
And we'll just put the year on the record. 
What's your full date of birth?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: January 9th, 1955.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Okay. And we'll X out or go off the record for 
next question.

entries.speaker: HEADING
entries.text: (Off-the-record discussion.)

entries.speaker: BY MR. KUMAR
entries.text: How tall are you, ma'am?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Five-three.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: And your present weight?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Like, 230.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Are you right-handed or left-handed?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Right.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Where were you born, ma'am?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: In Georgetown, South Carolina.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
And what year did you, I guess, move to 
Connecticut?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
1970 -- I think it was like -- oh, my God -- 
'71. I've been here so long.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: So 1971 possibly?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yeah.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Okay. All right. The address you just gave 
where you presently reside 180 Dogwood, who lives there 
with you?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Willie McCullough.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Is his name Willie or William, if you know?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Willie, W-i-l-l-i-e.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Thank you. What's your relationship with 
Mr. McCullough?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: We have a son together.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: And what is your son's name?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Kenya, K-e-n-y-a.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: And last name McCullough?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: McCullough, yes.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: And how old is Kenya?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: How old is he?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Yes.

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Forty-nine.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Any grandchildren?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Aside from Kenya, does Mr. McCullough have any 
other children?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: How many?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
Living, maybe I think six, if I'm not mistaken. 
Five or six.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
When was the last time anyone else lived with 
you two, of course other than yourself and 
Mr. McCullough?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: It's been several years.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Before 2023?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
All right. Any of the medication you took, have 
you taken it earlier today?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Okay. Does it affect your ability to remember 
anything?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: No. It just -- no.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Okay. Are you currently retired?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yes, I am.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: When did you retire?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Retired in 2021; right?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Okay. And what did you used to do before 
retiring?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: I worked for the State of Connecticut.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Doing what for them?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: A case worker.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Do you know what department for -- as a case 
worker?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Department of Social Services.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
And how many years did you work for -- we'll 
call it "DSS" for short?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yeah. Like about 33 and a half years.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Were you always a case worker?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
And what were your, I guess, day-to-day duties 
as a case worker?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
I would interact with clients. You know, assist 
them with, you know, whatever they needed, like, as far as 
services.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Help them get services?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
Yes. I would help them with the application 
process or -- you know, or they needed certain documents 
that they weren't able to get on their own, I would assist 
them in trying to get the documents so you can grant the 
case for them.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Okay. And what part of Connecticut did you work 
out of?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
Bridgeport. Well, Stamford -- started off in 
Stamford and Bridgeport.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Any other jobs since retiring in 2021?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
While working for the state, any part-time 
jobs?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
Actually, I did. I worked for People's United 
Bank in the collections department.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: What years were that?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: I think it was, like, around '88, '89.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Did you do that more than one year?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
I did. I worked for them for maybe -- well, 
first it was United, then Royal Bank of Scotland took it 
over. It went through a process. Maybe for, like, 14 
years.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
And that was while you were still working for 
the State?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Any other work that you recall?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Okay. What's your highest level of education, 
ma'am?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
A bachelor of science degree and a bachelor of 
religious education.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: So science and education?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yep.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
I'm sorry. The second degree was in 
education?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Religious education.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
When did you obtain those bachelors? What 
years, if you remember? I know it's been a while.

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: I know.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: You look very young, though.

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
Thank you. Okay. I want to say I think, gosh, 
back in '94 maybe, because I remember I had my son and I 
went back to school. Maybe somewhere.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Were they both from the same institution or 
college?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
No. My bachelor's of science I received that in 
Springfield, Massachusetts.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Which institution was that?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: University.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Which college?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Springfield.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Okay. Sorry. It's a city as well?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Oh, okay.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: And you said that was around '94?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
I may not have the dates right, but around, 
yes.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: And the religious bachelor's?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
That was Albany, New York, which is before 
that.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Was it part of the SUNY colleges in Albany or 
something else?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: No. It was part of something else. A church.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Did you ever work at a church or any other 
religious institution?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yes, but not for pay.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
And was it teaching Sunday school or something 
else?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yes. Sunday school teacher. Elder church.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Are you presently involved in any church?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Which church?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Resurrected Life Apostolic Church.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
I'm sorry. I got Resurrected Life. What was 
the other?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Apostolic.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Apostolic?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: And where is this church?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
2325 East Main Street in Bridgeport, 
Connecticut.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
And presently what do you do for the church or 
how are you involved?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Sunday school teacher. Elder.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
When you say "elder," what do you do for the 
elderly there?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
Whatever they need assistance with. I'm also a 
teacher. Teach.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Is it care as well or only teaching?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Basically teaching.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: And how long have you been doing this?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: For several years.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Since retirement?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Even before retirement.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Okay. Other than, of course, being in church on 
Sundays, does it require you be in church on other days as 
well?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
No. Basically, we -- just Sundays we -- we're 
basically on Zoom. I mean, I don't really do -- I do it, 
but I don't really do a lot anymore.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Understood. Are you on any Medicare, ma'am?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: What about social security?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Is it regular social security or disability or 
both?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Retirement.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
And what is your monthly stipend for social 
security?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Before or after taxes?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Whichever number you want to -- you're 
comfortable with giving.

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
I think it's 27 about. Yes. Roughly over 
2,700.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
$2,700 a month? You nodded. It has to be yes 
or no.

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
Oh, I'm sorry. I was calculating in my head. 
I'm sorry. Yes.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: And that 27, is it pretax or post tax?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Post.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Okay. Any other retirement pension or income?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
Yes. I get a pension from the State of 
Connecticut.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: And what is that per month?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
Before taxes -- now after taxes it's around 
4,100.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Did you say 21?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: And that's post taxes?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: After taxes.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Any other sources of income other than these 
two?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
All right. So if you're not doing the Zoom 
church meetings, how else do you pass your time normally, 
day-to-day basis?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
I read. I read a lot. Try to do house chores 
when I can.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
All right. Anything else? What do you do for 
fun other than read and likely church as well?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
Fun? To be honest, since this accident I don't 
know what fun is.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: What did you used to do before the accident?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Travel.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Where would you --

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
You know, I -- you know, I would get out and I 
would walk, you know, try and walk. You know, try to go 
out with friends.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
What else did you used to do before the 
accident? I got the travel, walking outside, hanging out 
with friends.

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Excuse me a minute.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: It's okay.

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
To be honest, before this -- since this 
accident, I don't really do anything other than really go 
to the doctor or try to go to a supermarket because -- 
sorry.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
If you want to take a break, Ms. Brown, we can. 
If you want to continue, that's okay too.

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: I'm good. I'm good. It's just --

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: I understand. It can be tough.

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: It's hard to explain it.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
As you're aware -- well, we'll go to the 
accident for a moment. Some of these questions I have to 
ask.
Have you ever been convicted of any crimes in 
Connecticut?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Filed bankruptcy in the last ten years?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
The accident that we're here for today, ma'am, 
when did that take place?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: May of 2023.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Was it May 20th?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
It was a weekend birthday. I think it was the 
2023. 2023.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: And where did the accident take place?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Off of Route 8. Around Exit 7. They changed

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text: BY MR. KUMAR:

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: How tall are you, ma'am?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: I'm sorry. The second degree was in

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: education?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: When you say "elder," what do you do for the

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: elderly there?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
Off of Route 8. Around Exit 7. They changed
the exits now.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Do you also drive, ma'am?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yes, I do.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
And back in May of 2023, did you have a valid
driver's license?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Any restrictions on your license for eyeglasses
or hearing?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
All right. Before the accident took place,
where were you coming from?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
We had stayed -- it was his birthday, so we took
a few days off and we were coming back home that day.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Okay. And do you know if you had traveled
outside of Connecticut or somewhere else?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: No. We were inside Connecticut.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Was it Mohegan Sun?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
Yes. Because his birthday, we went up and we
stayed, like, a couple nights.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
And this accident took place as you were coming
back home?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
Actually, we were, like, seven minutes, you
know, from the house, you know, on Exit 7.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
So just about to get home and then the accident
happens?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Okay. Again, I know -- I see you nodding.

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yes. I'm sorry.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: But you have to say yes or no. I apologize.

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
I'm sorry. You said that. Yes, as we were
getting off Exit 7, we were -- because traffic was backed
up. It was raining. We came to, like, almost like a
complete stop. And there was an SUV behind us and another
car behind the SUV, which triggered the three car.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
All right. So it was a three car total
accident; correct?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: What kind of vehicle were you in?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: He has an SUV.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Do you know if it's an Acura?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Acura. Yes.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Any reason Mr. McCullough was driving as opposed
to you?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
Because it's his SUV and men don't usually like
women driving their car.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Understood. I apologize for that. I
understand.
So he was in the driver's seat, you were in the
front passenger seat when the accident took place?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: And were you both wearing seat belts?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Always.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
All right. Had you already gotten off the exit
when the accident took place?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yes. We were right off the exit.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Were you still on the exit ramp or were you on
the private road by then?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: We were on the exit ramp.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Okay. So this accident takes place while you
were getting off the Route 8 but still on the exit ramp?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yes. Exit 7.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Okay. And that Exit 7, does that end with a
red -- like with a regular traffic light or a stop sign?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
It ends with a stop sign. A red light all the
way at the end.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
What were the traffic conditions, I guess, on
the exit?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
It was raining. Traffic was backed up. We were
all the way almost at the end of the exit and -- because
the girl that was behind us, she was in the SUV. So a guy
in the car came off the exit because it was -- again, it
was raining and plus he was going too fast. I mean, he
just -- but he hit her. You know, just caused a three-car
accident.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Okay. That ramp, is it -- does it slope
downwards or upwards or any way like that or is it flat?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: It's flat.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Does it turn to the right or left or anything
like that, or do you know?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
No. Because you get off on the right and it was
just a straight exit.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
All right. How many impacts did you feel to the
car you were in?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
Two, because I remember going forward when it
hit. At first I didn't realize what it was, what had
happened to us, because like I said we were almost like a
standstill. And I felt it in my back and my neck.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Okay. In terms of the physical car -- I'm going
to get to your body parts, of course, in a moment. How
many impacts did you feel to the Acura, the car you were
in?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: How many --

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Did you feel two?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
Okay. Since you put it that way, then I felt --
I still felt two.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Okay. Can you describe the first impact? From
what side of the car did you feel that?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: The back.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: And what about the second one?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
I understand what you're saying, but the back
again.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
When you say you "understand what I'm saying,"
did you feel a first impact and then your vehicle, the
Acura you were in, was struck again, or something else?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
No. I guess it's the way I'm explaining it. I
felt it in my back and then my neck. I went like that.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Just for the record, you're indicating that your
body moved forward and your neck moved forward and back.
Is that what you were demonstrating right now?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Okay. In terms of the physical impact between
the cars, was it just one impact from the back or did --
was your car hit more than once?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
Oh, okay. One. I'm thinking more about my
back.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
All right. And when you felt that one impact to
the back of the Acura, was the car you were in completely
stopped?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yes, it was.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
How many seconds was it stopped for before you
felt that impact?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
We were sitting there for probably 60 second or
more because, again, we couldn't go anywhere because the
traffic was backed up. Could have been longer than
that.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Now, how many cars, if you know, were between
that red light and in front of your car?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
I would say maybe five, six, if I'm judging it
right, because at the end there was a red light.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Now, when the Acura was struck from the back,
did it move in any direction? Was it pushed left? right?
forward?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Forward.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
In terms of distance, would it be a foot? five
feet? something else? Like, how much did it move
forward?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
As far as distance, I can't say; but as far as
impact, it moved.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Okay. Did you feel it jerk forward?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: I did.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Okay. And you're not able to tell me how far;
correct?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: No, I can't. I'm not --

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Immediately before feeling the impact, did you
hear any car horns or warning signs?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Did you hear any tire screeching sounds?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Not that I can recall.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: I've got to take a short break.

entries.speaker: HEADING
entries.text: (Recess: 12:52 p.m. to 12:57 p.m.)

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Ms. Brown, right before the break you had just
told me there were about five or six cars stopped ahead of
the car you were in; correct?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
And you were stopped for about 60 seconds when
you felt the impact to the back of your car. Yes?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
And it was raining at the time or was it raining
the entire time you were driving home?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
Pretty much the entire time we were driving
home.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Now, at any point before, let's say, 24 hours
before this accident, did Mr. McCullough drink any
alcohol, if you know?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: He doesn't drink.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Any recreational drugs 24 hours before this
accident?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Was he eating or drinking anything while driving
immediately before this accident took place?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Talking on the cell phone?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Do you know if the Acura was displaying any GPS
directions?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Immediately before the impact took place, were
you looking ahead or where were you looking, if you
remember?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Ahead.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Were you able to see if there were any vehicles
stopped while you were stopped for about 60 seconds?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
Yes. Because, again, it was a red light and the
traffic is backed up.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
And you said you saw the vehicles behind you.
Did you look, turn around turning your neck, or were you
able to see it through I guess your driver's side
mirror -- I mean passenger's side mirror?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yes. The mirror.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Okay. And you described the other vehicle, the
one that was right behind you as an SUV just like the
Acura?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
It was an SUV. I don't remember what make
or --

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Do you remember the color?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
I'm not sure if it was red or not. I don't
remember. But I do remember her getting out and getting
in the car with us until the police came.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Okay. So immediately after you feel that one
impact to the back of your car, what happens next? Does
she come over to you or what else happens? Something
else?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
No. We saw her. She got out of the car and I
believe he got out and they exchanged information. And
then she came over to our car, truck, and pretty much she
was just -- she was out of it too, explaining what
happened. You know, and then --

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Did she speak to both of you or just
Mr. McCullough?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Well, both of us.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Okay.

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
And then she had -- because he was going to get
the information too, but she said she had already gotten
his information the guy in the car.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Did she tell you what conversation she had with
the other gentleman in the third vehicle?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
No. All she said was that she had gotten his
information. So we didn't -- you know, Willie didn't get
out to get the information since she already had the
information. And then she volunteered to give us her
information and the other guy's information and that --
she called the police.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Did she apologize to you about the accident at
all?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
Well, she's a little -- she was a little upset
because -- yes. Yes, she was --

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
What conversation do you recall -- I know you're
not going to remember exactly every detail because it
happened a while ago, but whatever you do remember what
was that?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
No. She was just surprised, you know, that
she -- that she was in an accident, that the guy hit her,
and that she was on her way to a wedding and she lived in
Massachusetts.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Can you describe that young lady for me?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
To be honest, no, other than Caucasian. I think
she was a blond.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
In terms of age, younger, older, or something
else?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
She was younger. She had to have been in her
20s probably. Because it was raining and she didn't know
what she was going to do and her car was smoking, so we
offered to let her sit, you know, in the back seat -- she
called her mom -- until the police came.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
So she sat in your vehicle or Mr. McCullough's
vehicle for a while?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yes, because it was raining.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Did she explain to you how the accident
happened?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
She didn't go into any details. It was just
more she couldn't believe that the guy hit her. That he
ran in the back of her. That's what happened. Yeah. And
then, yeah, she did say because he pushed her into,
you
know --

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: So her vehicle was pushed into your vehicle?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
It was a three car. I know we had stopped -- to
my recollection, I don't remember if her car was still
moving when he hit her, but I know we couldn't go anywhere
because of the traffic, the cars in front of us.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Okay. Just going back for a moment.
So you and Mr. Willie, Mr. McCullough, were
stopped for about a minute, is that fair to say, or a
little bit less or a little bit more?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yeah. It had stopped.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
All right. The first time you saw the vehicle
that was behind you of this young lady, do you know if it
was completely stopped or coming to a stop, if you know?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Again, I don't know.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Now, do you know if that vehicle rear-ended your
vehicle before the other accident took place?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: You mean before he hit her?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Before the other rear-end accident, yes.

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
To be honest, I'm not sure, but I don't think
so.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: What makes you not think so?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
Because the way he -- just when we got out of
the car, we just -- I'm no traffic expert, but I took
pictures and it's just the way his car hit hers.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
What did the pictures show? Were the cars still
touching or did they show damage for all the vehicles or
something else?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: How many photos do you remember taking?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Maybe four or five, six something.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: And did you take them using your cell phone?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yes, I did.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
And were you able to take photos of the other
vehicle, the third one as well, before it left the
accident scene?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Do you recall the make or model or any other
description of that third vehicle?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
I think it was an Audi. I think it was an Audi.
I'm not really good with that.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Was it an SUV like the Acura or a smaller sedan
or something else?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: No. A sedan. A car.

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: The color?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
I believe his -- may have been red. I saw the
red.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Okay. I know -- is it fair to say you didn't
speak to the other driver of the Audi at the accident
scene?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: No, I didn't.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Okay. Was he a Caucasian male, a black male, or
something else?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: He was a black male.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
In terms of age, again, 20s? 40s? 50s?
Something like that?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
He was a young guy. Maybe 30s, 20s. Late 20s.
I'm not sure.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Do you remember calling 911 from your phone?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: No, I didn't because she did.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
And when she did, was she already in the back
seat of, I guess, Mr. McCullough's SUV?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: No. Actually, she called before she got in.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Okay. Did she let you know she called them
already?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yes, she did.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Now, how long did it take for the police to get
to the accident scene?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
Could have been 30 or more, 30 minutes or
more.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
What do you remember doing for those 30 minutes
at the accident scene?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
I guess we were all -- you know, just couldn't
believe we were in an accident. We were just talking.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Did the young woman stay in your car until the
police got there?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
She did because it was raining and we didn't
want her standing outside.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Okay. Any other conversation other than about
the accident?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
No. We didn't really talk about the accident
again because she was just -- she was upset.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Okay. Anyone make any complaints of -- whether
it was you or Mr. McCullough or this young lady about any
aches or pains because of the accident?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
At the time, I cannot recall. Well, when the
car hit, I do. That's what made me -- I couldn't believe
we were in an accident. I remember I heard the boom and I
felt it because I told Will, I said, Oh, my goodness, I
said, I felt that in my back.
He said -- he looked in the mirror and he said,
Someone hit us.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
All right. So that impact in the back of the
Acura, did it feel heavy for you?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: The hitting my back?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Well, the back of the Acura.

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
Yes, it did. I'm sorry. I'm kind of -- I
should have told you, I'm kind of groggy because of the
pregabalin.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Are you okay to continue, though? Or if you
want, we can do it another day.

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: I'm good. A little spacey, but I'm good.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Okay. Now, in terms of how your body moved -- I
know you were describing it earlier. Can you describe it
one more time how your body moved after you felt that
initial impact to the car?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yeah. It went forward.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
And as you went forward, did your -- any part of
your body hit anything inside of the Acura?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: No. I do not recall.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Once the police officers got there, did they ask

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
Once the police officers got there, did they ask
you if you were hurt in this accident?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text: Pardon me?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text: He did.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
What do you remember reporting to that 
question?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text:
No.  He asked if we needed to go to the hospital 
and we said no because we didn't feel anything broken at 
that time.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
Even though you declined going to the hospital, 
did you report any injuries to the police officer?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text:
No.  As I recall, I don't recall him asking us 
about any injuries other than if we needed to go to the 
hospital.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
While waiting for the police officers, did you 
report any aches or pains to Mr. McCullough?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text: No.  We didn't really talk about that.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
Did he make any complaints to you about any 
aches or pains?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text:
I don't recall because we were just, you know, 
just waiting -- trying to wait for the policeman.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
Okay.  Do you know if the car behind the young 
lady was driving, the second car, did the airbags in that 
car go off or blow up?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text:
I don't know because I didn't go to her car -- 
truck.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
Was any car, as far as you know, towed from the 
accident scene?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text:
Not that I'm aware of.  I shouldn't say no 
because he gave us clearance to leave.  So we left her 
there with the policeman.  The other guy took off 
previously.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
So you left before the second car left; 
correct?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text: Yes.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
Okay.  Once you got the clearance to go home, 
did Mr. McCullough then just drive home?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text: Yeah.  We went straight home.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
When was the first time you started feeling any 
aches or pains after the accident?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text: The next morning.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text: What did you start feeling?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text:
My back.  I went to -- I think it was the next 
week I went to the walk-in to --

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
So did the lower back start hurting the next day 
or something else?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text:
No, it started hurting the next day.  That's 
what prompted me to go to the walk-in.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
Did you go to the walk-in clinic right after -- 
the day after the accident?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text:
It was either the day after or maybe a couple 
days.  But it wasn't far from it.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
And the next morning or the next day did 
Mr. McCullough make any complaints of pain?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text: Yes.  His back too.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
Who's the -- what was the name of the clinic he 
first went to?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text: Orthopedic Specialty Group out of --

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text: Did you both go together?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text:
When we first went there, no, no, I went by 
myself the first time.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text: Were you able to drive yourself there?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text: Yes, I did.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text: Had you ever been to the clinic before?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text:
No.  I've never been to the clinic.  I had a 
doctor there.  I was seeing a doctor there that retired or 
relocated.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
Which doctor were you seeing there at that 
facility before this accident took place?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text: Offhand, I don't remember his name offhand.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text: What were you seeing that doctor for?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text:
I started going to therapy.  Was it therapy?  I 
forgot when I started going to him.  I think it was --

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
Now, this is -- again, I just want to be clear.  
Before this accident took place you were going to them for 
physical therapy?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text:
Yes.  But it wasn't, like, an old time type of 
therapy.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
Do you recall why you needed that physical 
therapy?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text:
Because I work -- I was, you know, sick a lot.  
So my doctor suggested -- more of a suggestion that 
therapy would help.  I think it was Bendaglass.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text: The name of the doctor?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text:
Yes.  I think that was his name at the time.  He 
relocated or retired.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
As best as you can spell it for me, Ms. Brown, 
please.

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text: I think it's B-e-n-d-a-g-l-a-s-s.  I'm not sure.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text: Again, he's since moved practice or retired?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text: I'm not sure which one.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
And you said the physical therapy was due to 
issues during when you were working; is that fair?

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
Okay.  What sort of issues were you having prior 
to this accident while working?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text: Just sitting sometimes.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
Sitting for a long period of time or just 
sitting at all was an issue?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text: Just sometimes.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
Was it the time you sat or just sitting in 
general?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text: I think a little of both.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
Okay.  And what would that cause, back pain or 
something else?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text: Sometimes back, yeah.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
How long did you get that physical therapy 
for?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text:
Maybe about two, three weeks.  And that was 
it.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
What would they do for you for that physical 
therapy?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text: Basically just stretching or heat, you know.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
Did they just work on your lower back or other 
body parts as well?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text: No.  Just lower back.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
When was the last time you were at that facility 
before the accident took place?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text:
I don't recall because I wasn't having a problem 
with my back like that.  It was every now and again.  It 
wasn't consistent, you know.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
Did you ever treat at Orthopedic Specialty Group 
for your neck or cervical spine?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text:
I think -- did he work on my spine?  It was more 
on my back.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
And do you remember getting any MRIs done before 
this accident of your neck or back?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text:
I think x-ray maybe.  I'm not sure about the 
MRI.  Maybe.  It's been a while.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text: What was the x-ray for, your neck or back?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text:
I know when I went there when I had the accident 
they took x-rays I think of both, I believe.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
I'm going to get to the accident.  I'm just for 
now before this accident because we were talking about you 
visiting the facility before.  
Do you remember getting x-rays or MRIs of your 
neck?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text:
I don't recall getting MRIs of my neck.  But my 
back I know I got x-rays.  I'm not sure.  I know I've had 
an MRI since.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
Okay.  Any other treatment other than, of 
course, the physical therapy at that facility for you, for 
your neck or back?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text:
Dr. Saba, he did try injections, but it -- it 
didn't work on me.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
Okay.  And are those injections, again, before 
May of 2023?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text:
I want to say one probably -- maybe, like, four, 
and then the accident one after.  And then -- I tell him 
that they just -- they didn't work.  And he said some 
people they just don't work on.  And that's when he put me 
on the pregabalin.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
Okay.  Now, in May of 2019 -- so that's about 
four years before this accident took place -- do you 
remember going to Orthopedic Specialty Group for a neck 
issue?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text:
Okay.  Yes, I do.  But, again, it wasn't, like, 
all the time.  I had a couple doctors that went through -- 
that left.  I don't remember if it was Bendaglass or 
another doctor that I saw.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
Okay.  Did you ever get any trigger point 
injections for your neck or back before this accident took 
place?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text:
For my neck, no, I've never had injection in my 
neck.  Again, for my back, as best as I can remember, 
maybe one.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
Okay.  Do you remember getting injections back 
in June of 2021?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text: For?

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text: For your neck or back.

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text:
If I was seeing Saba again, maybe one, because 
I'm the type of person I don't like needles so I would not 
let him continue to stick me knowing that they weren't 
working.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
So, again, before this accident the only 
injection you remember is maybe one to your lower back and 
nothing else?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text:
Yes, because he never gave me an injection in my 
neck.  He's not a neck doctor.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
Okay.  Now, what about July of 2021, do you 
remember another injection?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text: In my neck or back?

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
Back.  Because you already said you never had 
any in your neck; correct?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text: No.  That I can recall, no.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
Okay.  In terms of your lower back, did you have 
one in July of '21?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text:
Again, I may or -- I may have if it was with 
Dr. Saba.  And that was before 2023.  So like I said, 
maybe once because -- twice because it didn't work on 
me.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text: What about February of 2022?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text: No.  Not for injections.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text: Okay.

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text:
I saw him, yes, but maybe -- not for 
injection.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text: All right.  How about August of 2022?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text: I -- you can pull my records.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
It's what you remember, ma'am.  I'm not trying 
to trick you.  If you don't remember, that's okay to tell 
me you don't remember.

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text:
I don't remember.  But I know I don't like 
needles.  I just would not let him continue to stick me 
with them.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
Do you recall getting an injection in November 
of 2022?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text: Nope.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text: What about December of 2022?

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
The physical therapy facility that I have, it 
says "OSG," which standards for Orthopedic Specialty Group 
Physical and Occupational Therapy, starting visits were 
back in June of 2019.  
Do you remember starting physical therapy

entries.text:
It could have been around that time.  I don't 
remember right now.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
It looks like up until the accident took place 
you were still getting physical therapy until May 18th of 
2023.

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text: I may have, but I don't recall.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
This accident date that I have is May 20th, 
2023.  Do you have any reason to refute that that's not 
the date?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text: What, the accident that we had here?

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text: That we're here for today.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text: May 20th; correct?

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
And the last visit I have with the physical 
therapy facility is May 18th of 2023.  So two days before 
this accident.  Do you remember going there?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text:
In all honest, no, I don't remember going there.  
Three years ago.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
Is it fair to say two days before the accident 
you were likely at Mohegan Sun?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text:
Well, I know I was at Mohegan Sun.  I told you.  
We were coming back from his birthday.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
What about the week before May 13 of 2023, do 
you remember getting physical therapy then?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text: I don't remember.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
Do you remember any physical therapy visit let's 
say a week or two before this incident took place that 
we're here for today?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text: No, I don't.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
All right.  So after this incident that we're 
here for today of May 20th of 2023, did you go back to the 
physical therapy facility for continued physical 
therapy?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text: After May 20, 2023?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text:
No.  I went to Connecticut Spine.  I think it 
was Connecticut Spine Institute.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
Okay.  And the doctor I have there is Dr. Glenn 
Chasanoff.  Do you remember that name?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text: Yes.  He's the doctor there.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
What did the -- that doctor do for you?  What 
kind of treatment did he recommend or she?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text:
Massage.  He did treatment of the lower lumbar, 
heat, and gel.  I think they call it, like, 
electroshock.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
All right.  Just going back to Connecticut Spine 
for a moment.  At the initial appointment, what complaints 
did you have for them?  What hurt or what did you explain

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text: With Dr. Chasanoff?

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text: I have Dr. Chasanoff at CT Spine.

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text:
Chasanoff.  My lower back.  And I kept telling 
him I started feeling sensation going down from my back 
into my legs.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text: Was it a tingling sensation or something else?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text:
No.  It was something else.  Something I never 
felt before.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
How would you describe it?  Is it like when your 
leg falls asleep like that, or something else?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text:
It's like -- it's -- it's like when my leg -- it 
started on my right leg.  It was still -- it was like it 
would be moving even though it was still.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
Did anyone diagnosis you with restless leg 
syndrome or no?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text:
No, because I never had a problem with my 
legs.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
Not before, but after the accident did any 
doctor suggest to you that you may have restless leg 
syndrome?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text: No.  Dr. Saba, he told me it was the nerves.

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text:
That's why he put me on the pregabalin to help 
with the sensation because it was hard to sleep at

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text: night.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
Just going back to CT Spine for a moment again.  
How many months in total did you treat there?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text:
I would say maybe like five and a half months, 
maybe six.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text: Did that treatment help at all?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text:
Therapy is like a Band-Aid.  At the time it kind 
of like helped a little.  But sitting here today, I will 
tell you no.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
When was the last time you remember going to 
Connecticut Spine?  Was it somewhere in October of 2023?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text: Sounds about right.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
And since October of 2023, when was the next 
time you went to any doctor in relationship to this 
accident, of course?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text:
I had therapy -- again, Dr. Saba suggested 
someone he knew in Connecticut -- or Stratford, 
Connecticut.  I'm sorry.  I don't recall his name right 
now.  But I went to him for, like -- I would say roughly, 
like, five or six weeks.  And he basically did the same 
thing to -- it was the bike, the electrical shocks, the 
gel, the massage.  And it was just temporary.  It didn't 
work.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
So Dr. Saba asked you to go to additional 
physical therapy?

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
And do you know the name of that physical 
therapy facility?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text:
Offhand, I don't know -- I don't recall the name 
of the place.  I could get it.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
Okay.  Did any doctor, whether it's Dr. Saba or 
anyone else, send you for any MRIs?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text:
Well, yes.  Again, Dr. Saba, he just -- he 
didn't know how else to help me.  So he -- I don't know 
the doctor's name.  So he had me -- I saw another doctor 
who they had me do, like, an MRI and -- on my back.  And 
because my nerves, they're just so bad.  She said the only 
way that they can try -- no guarantees -- to correct this 
is through surgery.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text: Was that Dr. Saba?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text:
No, it wasn't Dr. Saba.  It was Dr. -- it's a 
funny name.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
I have a few names.  You let me know if it's one 
of them.

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text: I forgot the name.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text: I have a Dr. Troy Glaser, G-l-a-s-e-r.

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text: No.  I don't remember that.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
What about Dr. John Awad, A-w-a-d, the last 
name?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text: Yes.  Awad.  Yes, I saw him.  I think Awad and

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text: the other doctor.  They work together.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
Another doctor name is Raj, R-a-j, last name 
Gala, G-a-l-a.

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text:
Yes.  He was a -- I think he was like a third -- 
you know, a second opinion.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
Okay.  So is it Dr. Awad or Dr. Gala that 
recommended the surgery, or both?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text:
No.  I think it was Dr. Awad.  I'm not sure who 
recommended -- I think Dr. Awad was, like, the second 
opinion.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
And did Dr. Awad or any other doctor tell you 
why -- first of all, what type of surgery did they 
recommend?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text:
Back surgery where they would have to go in, 
like, reconstruct two, three discs in my back.  So the 
nerves can -- it's like whatever is going on, it's like 
it's pinching the nerves.  And when that happens, I don't 
feel sensation in my legs or my feet.  
I think -- she went into details to alleviate 
the pressure they would have to -- it just build a cage 
for the disc.  I just can't see myself doing it.  Not at 
this age.  It's just too risky.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
Okay.  Now, did Dr. Awad or anyone else tell you 
you would need some hardware placed in your lumbar spine 
or lower back, meaning plates or screws?

entries.speaker: THE WITNESS
entries.text: Yes.  Yes.  That was the part.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
And you said the second opinion was by a 

different doctor.  Who was that?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: I'm not sure of Awad -- not Awad -- Raj.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Raj Gala.

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
He was the second opinion, I think.  Awad was 

the first.  But there's another doctor that works with 

Awad.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Is it Dr. Judith Gorlick, G-o-r --

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yes.  Gorlick.  I think that's her.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: -- l-i-c-k.

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
Yes.  I think it's her.  And she's the one that 

would basically --

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Did any doctor tell you that the back surgery 

was -- you'd need the back surgery because of your 

injuries in the car accident?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
No.  I don't recall that.  All I recall is she 

telling me about the -- what's going to happen if I don't.  

What's going to -- might happen if I do.  So it's just --

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
So other than the physical therapy, of course, 

and you following with these doctors, you said you had one 

injection after this accident by Dr. Saba to your lower 

back; is that accurate?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
I don't recall when -- I really -- I don't 

recall.  But he has all my records.  I just know I never 

had no more than two, if three, no, because they don't 

work on me.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Now, any recommendation for surgery for your 

neck?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Because of my age --

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
All right.  Did any doctor tell you that your 

injuries were -- or your -- the way your back appeared it 

was due to your age or was it because of the car accident, 

if they commented on it at all?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
I don't ever recall them saying -- I don't 

remember them saying it in that exact term.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
All right.  Any doctors that you saw because of 

your injuries in May of 2023 to present that we haven't 

spoken about yet?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: No.  Those are --

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Those are the only ones that --

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: All right.

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: -- over the last several months that I've seen.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Now, at any point before, of course, this 

accident going back to the prior visits with the 

Orthopedic Specialty for neck, do you remember having any 

issues with a neck spasm or neck pain in May of 2019?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
I had problems, you know, before.  I think those 

prompted me to go over there.  And like I said, the 

therapy and it kind of like, you know -- but it wasn't an 

every day type of pain.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
As a result of the May 2023 accident, what 

injuries are you claiming?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
As a result of the May 2023 accident, I claim 

the injury of my back.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Lower back?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
My lower back is -- that accident brought on 

such a sciatica in my body.  It goes in my lower back, 

down.  Like I said, I first started therapy at CT.  I told 

Dr. Chasanoff about it.  It started in my right leg and 

then it moved down to my foot, right foot.  Then now it's 

on both sides and it goes down in both legs, my feet.  I 

can only stand so long.  I can't even walk across the 

street to the gas station over there without stopping 

because the nerves won't let me.  And because the nerve 

is -- which they told me it's weakening my strength, it's 

like my legs, they're not really supporting me right.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Okay.  Just a slight repetition, but lower back, 

of course, continues to hurt and there's a sensation that 

goes down your right leg to your right foot and now it's 

both legs; is that accurate?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
Right.  It's both legs.  And it's not -- it's 

not a foot, it's feet now.  My feet, they're constantly 

numb, and legs.  I just saw my doctor Monday.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Who's that?  Which doctor?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
Saba.  I saw his assistant.  She does the 

refills.  And, you know, they went up on my medication.  I 

don't want to take a higher drug.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Who's your primary care physician, Ms. Brown?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Dr. Kulakov.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Please spell it for me?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
It's weird doctors.  I have to get it for you 

because he has such a funny name.  Give me a second.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Sure.

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
Sorry.  I always carry this because -- okay.  

Salva, first same S-a-l-v-a, Salva, Kulakov, 

K-u-l-a-k-o-v.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: That's your primary care physician?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
And how long has Dr. Kulakov been your primary 

care physician?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
I would say, like, a couple years now.  And he's 

the one that's telling me my window is closing for 

surgery.

entries.text: Can we go off for a moment?

entries.text: Oh, yes.

entries.text:

those complaints?

entries.text: Pardon me?

other doctors.  And he said because of my age, if I was 

going to have this surgery, I should do it now because the 

window's closing.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
So he said if you're thinking of surgery, get it 

sooner rather than later?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
Yes, because of my age.  Because I guess -- and 

the rehab and the --

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Okay.  Who was your primary care physician 

before Dr. Kulakov?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Dr. Anthony Ciccaglione.

entries.text: Are you able to spell that last name for us?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yes.  C-i-c-c-h-e-l-i-o-n-e[sic].

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: And where was Dr. Ciccaglione's office?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
One's located on Main Street in Bridgeport and 

he also has one in Milford, Connecticut.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
And did you just change doctors or did that 

doctor retire?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: No.  I changed doctors.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
How long was Dr. Anthony Ciccaglione your 

primary care physician?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: What does "several" mean for you?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
I would say maybe about eight -- about eight 

years.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Was Dr. Kulakov made aware of this auto 

accident, the one you're here for today?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
I don't recall.  I'm pretty sure.  I complained 

a lot.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
What about Dr. Anthony Ciccaglione, was he aware 

of this car accident?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: No, because he wasn't my doctor.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Okay.  So when this accident took place, it was 

Dr. Kulakov was your primary care physician?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Right.  It was Dr. Kulakov.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Was Dr. Kulakov aware of your prior back 

complaints before this accident?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
No, because he's been -- he's only been my 

doctor a couple years, Kulakov, my primary.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Okay.  I was talking about Dr. Anthony 

Ciccaglione.  Was that doctor aware of your prior lower 

back pain?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
I want to say not really -- I'm not sure because 

although he was my primary, he wasn't --

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Did you change practices because of his care?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: He wasn't thorough enough.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Did you change practice from Ciccaglione's 

practice to Dr. Kulakov because Dr. Ciccaglione wasn't 

thorough?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
Yeah.  Yeah.  Because I was getting older and I 

wanted a more in-depth.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Understand.

entries.speaker: MR. KUMAR
entries.text:
Counsel, I don't believe 

we have records for either primary care 

physician.  We'll follow up in writing for 

both.

entries.text:
Q    So we know definitely lower back you're alleging 

it's gotten at least worse, is that fair to say because of 

the car accident, or no?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Do you have any complaints of your neck because 

of the May 2023 accident?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
My neck is stiff.  I can only turn my head so 

far.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: It's a limited movement of neck?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Very limited.  I have to turn my body.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Okay.  And did you ever have any issues with

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
I had some stiffness.  Nothing major.  I went to 

therapy, but --

entries.text:
Is that the physical therapy you were previously 

telling me about?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: OSG?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
And you said it's as a result of sitting at your 

desk.  Did you file any workers' compensation suit or 

claim against the State of Connecticut?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yes, I did, for carpal tunnel.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: What year was that?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
I don't remember the year.  Maybe '21, maybe 

'19, '20.

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: 2020 or 2021 maybe.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Did you need surgery to correct the carpal 

tunnel, or no?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
So other than the workers' comp claim for the 

carpal tunnel, did you have either claim for back or neck 

pain?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
There was a claim for my back, neck, but I 

never -- I never -- he never gave me any injections or 

anything because I didn't want that.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Okay.  When did you first make any claims for 

your neck or back through workers' comp?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: I don't recall.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Was it --

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: But that's --

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Go ahead.

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
But maybe that's the therapy that you saw at 

OSG.  Or I'm not sure.  I don't recall.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Okay.  We spoke about therapy.  I was just 

seeing if you filed any claim, a workers' comp claim with 

the State of Connecticut.

Do you remember doing that for your neck or 

back?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
For my neck I did, yes.  I used to see at OSG, 

he's no longer there.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Okay.  And do you recall what years that was?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: No, I don't recall what year.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Do you know how many years before the 2023 

accident?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
No.  I had therapy for my back then too.  But, 

again, it's nothing like now.  It happened, it cleared up, 

and I was doing fine.  I was walking fine.  You know, 

everything until I had that accident.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Okay.  Were you getting -- if you remember, 

let's say a week before this accident took place, were you 

getting any physical therapy, whether it's for your neck 

or back?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
I may have.  Like I said, I do not remember.  

But if I was getting therapy then, then my records will 

show it.  But I don't remember.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
What would the therapy be for?  For your neck or 

back?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
Because of the therapy, the way they do it, it 

may have been for -- probably my back -- I'm not sure 

which one.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
In terms of any incidents after this accident, 

May 2023 accident, did you have any other falls or 

incidents where you hurt your neck or back again?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Nope.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Did you have to spend any money out of your 

pocket for any of your treatment?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
In terms of activities -- I know we started a 

little bit with activity.  What is it that you were able 

to do without any issues before this accident took place 

that you can't do at all because of the May 2023 

accident?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
I could walk, which I would do two, three times 

a week.  I would be able to walk.  I could go to the 

supermarket without it being a struggle.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Okay.  I'm going to stop you just for a moment.  

So right now I'm looking for activities.

I understand you can still walk even if it's for 

one minute; is that fair to say?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Fair to say.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text:
Okay.  So what are the activities that you can't 

do at all?  I'm going to get to difficult or more 

challenging ones soon.

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: That I can't do or can?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Cannot do at all.

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
Cannot do at all.  Mop my floor.  The stairs is

entries.text: What else that you can't do at all?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
I know it's not an activity, but sleep.  It's -- 

very rarely sleep through the night.

entries.text:
Okay.  So stuff you can't do at all is mopping 

the floor.  Is there anything else you can't do at all?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text:
I can -- I still have to cook but, you know, I 

take my time.  But it's the standing.  That's what it is.

entries.text:
Have you hired anyone to help mop the floor or 

do you still do it with difficulty or did Mr. McCullough 

help or someone else?
